# About {.unnumbered}

A worked book for empirical asset pricing using Python Polars and local WRDS
Parquet files. The chapters build from size portfolios to factor adjustment,
double sorts, and Fama–MacBeth regression, inspired by Bali, Engle, and Murray's *Empirical Asset Pricing: The Cross Section
of Stock Returns*. [AnomalyLab](https://github.com/FinPhD/AnomalyLab) is an
independent numerical reference, not a reader dependency.

The methods examples compare implementations on the same inputs. The final
chapter compares reconstructed size summaries with the published Table 9.1.
The book does not redistribute WRDS data.


## Data vintages

These are the source update dates recorded in the Parquet metadata, read by
[db2pq](https://iangow.github.io/db2pq/). They are not the sample end dates
or the dates the files were copied. In particular, the Table 9.1 replication
uses a later export of legacy CRSP (SIZ), not the original 2016 book vintage.

```{python}
#| echo: false

import polars as pl
from db2pq import pq_last_modified

tables = [
    ("crsp", "msf"),
    ("crsp", "msenames"),
    ("crsp", "msf_v2"),
    ("crsp", "dsf_v2"),
    ("ff", "factors_monthly"),
]

pl.DataFrame({
    "Table": [f"{schema}.{name}" for schema, name in tables],
    "metadata": [pq_last_modified(name, schema) for schema, name in tables],
}).select(
    "Table",
    pl.col("metadata").str.extract(r"Updated (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})")
    .fill_null("Not recorded").alias("Source updated"),
)
```
